FOREWORD

This Indian Standard ( Part 1 ) (First Revision ) which is identical with IS0 8490 : 1986 `Metallic materials - Sheet and stripModified Erichsen cupping test' issued by the International Organization for Standardization ( IS0 ), was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on the recommendations of the Mechanical Testing of Metals Sectional Committee ( MTD 3 ) and approval of the Metallurgical Engineering Division Council. This standard was first published in 1982 superseding IS 1756 : 1974 `Method for modified Erichsen cupping test for steel sheet and strip ( first revision ). The present revision has been brought out to affect harmonization with International Standards. This standard, earlier published as IS 10175 : 1982 `Method for modiiied Erichsen cupping test for metallic sheet and strip', is now being issued in two parts. While this part of the standard covers method of modified Erichsen cupping test for sheets and strips having thickness up to 2 mm, Part 2 intends to cover thickness 2 mm and above. The text of IS0 Standard has been approved as suitable for publication without deviations. Some terminology conventions are, however, not used in Indian Standards. Attention is especially drawn to the following: a) Wherever the words `International should be read as `Indian Standard'. b) Comma practice Standard' appear, referring in Indian as Indian Standard identical with those to this standard, they

PART 1 ( THICKNESS Up To 2 MILLIMETRES

1

Scope and field of application

2

Principle

This International Standard specifies a method for determining the ability of metallic sheets and strips having a thickness from 0.2 up to 2 mm and a width of 90 mm or more to undergo plastic deformation in stretch drawing.

Forming a cup shape by pressing a punch with a spherical end against a clamped test piece between a blank holder and a die until a through crack appears. The measured depth of the cup is the result of the test based on the movement of the-punch.

NOTE - The test is referred to as the modified Erichsen cupping test as, in the test as originally introduced, no blank holder pressure was used but, in the interests of obtaining greater consistency of results, this was changed.

4 4.1

Testing equipment

4.5

The Erichsen cupping test shall be carried out on a machine equippsd'with a die, punch and blank holder with dimensions and tolerances as shown in the figure.

The distance from the axis of the die to the centre of the spherical part of the punch shall be less than 0.1 mm throughout its range of movement in use. The surfaces of the blank holder and of the die in contact with the test piece shall be plane and perpendicular to the axis of movement of the punch. These surfaces shall be parallel within 0.01 mm. The machine shall ensure holding the test piece with a constant holding force of approximately 10 kN.

4.7

4.2

The comtruction of the machine shall be such that it is possible to observe the outsideof the test piece during the test to be able to determine the instant when a through crack appears

4.8

4.3

A through crack is a crack which goes through the full thickness of the test piece and is just sufficiently wide to allow liiht to pass through part of its length. The machine shall be equipped with a gauge for measuring the movement of the punch with a scale division of 0,l mm.

4.9

Measurement of the movement of the punch takes place from the point where it initially touches the surface of the test piece.

4.4

4.6

5
5.1

Test piece

The dii, the blank holder and the punch shall be suffi ciently rigid not to deform appreciably during the test. The Vickers hardness of working surfaces of the die, the blank holder and the punch shall be at least 750 HV 30. 4.5.1 The punch shall not turn during the test.

The test piece shall be flat and of such dimensions that the centre of any cup is not less than 45 mm from any edge of the test piece, and not less than 90 mm from the centre of the nearest cup.

4.5.2 The working surface of the punchshall be spherical and polfshed. This spherical portion shall be in contact with the test piece during the test.

5.2 The preparation of the test piece shall not produce bn the edges any burr or distortion which would prevent it being placed in the machine and which could interfere with the performance of the test. Dimensionsin millimetrss

5.3 Before testing, the test piece shall not be submitted to
any hammering or hot or cold working.

6.6 Procaed with forming the cup smoothly at a rate between
5 and 20 mm/min. Towards the end of the operation, reduce the speed to-the vicinity of the lower limit in order to determine accurately the moment v&en a through crack appears.

6

Procedure

8.1 In general, the test shall be carried out at ambient
temperature within the limits of 10 to 35 OC. The test carried out under controlled conditions shall be made at a temperature of 23 f 5 oc. 6.2 Determine the thickness of the test piece to the nearest 0,Ol mm.

6.7 Terminate the movement of the punch at the instant
when a crack appears through the full thickness of the test piece.

8.8

Measure the depth of penetration to the nearest 0.1 mm. This depth expressed in millimetres is the value of the Erichsen cupping index IE.

6.3 Before operating the machine, lightly grease the two
faces of the test piece and the punch with graphite grease. For the recommended composition of the graphii grease, see the annex. By agreement, another _tvpaof lubricant may be used. a) reference to this International Standard; identification of the test piece; thickness of the test piece; n/pe of lubricant used;

7

Test report

The test report shall include at least the following information :

6.4 Clamp the test piece between the blank holder and the
die. The blank holder force shall be approximately 10 kN. 6.8 Bring the punch without shock into contyt with the test piece. Make the measurement of penetration from this point.

b) cl d)

e) value of the Erichsen cupping index.

Annex Recommended composition of the graphite grease
(seeg.3)

(This annex is given for information only.)

It is known that the results of tests depend on the type of grease used. One representative grease which is known to be suitable has the following characteristics, as determined bv the relevant material specifications. The grease consists of calcium soap, refined mineral oil and flake graphite. It should be free from corrosive matter, grit resin, wax and fillers. The grease and its components should conform to the requirements shown in table 2.

Standard Mark

I
The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau ojzndian Standards Acr, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 1
